file_metadata.conversation_model_note: All meetings and email correspondence are strictly between the relationship manager and the client. No other bank staff appear as participants or correspondents.
file_metadata.content_note: This file contains verbatim transcripts and raw email bodies only. No pre-computed summaries, action items, owners or due dates are supplied. All such output must be derived by the agent and cited back to a meeting_id plus transcript seq, or a thread_id plus message_id.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Morning Erik, thanks for making the time.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Morning Priya. Can you hear me alright? I'm in the car.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Loud and clear. So this is the annual review. I'll take you through last year and the positioning, and then I know you had a couple of things you wanted to raise.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Yeah, two things. But go ahead first.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Okay. So 2025 finished up broadly in line. The dynamic mandate did what it should. The drag was — well, you know where the drag was.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: China.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: China.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Yeah. Look, I want to talk about that properly. Because every time we have this call it's the same conversation and the number doesn't move.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That's fair.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: How much do I actually have in China? Because when I look at the statement it tells me Hong Kong is — I don't know, two point something percent? That can't be right. It doesn't feel like two percent.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: It's not two percent. That's the thing. The country allocation table only picks up the directly held equities. The listed stuff — Alibaba, Bank of China, the tower company, SMIC, ICBC, CCB.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: And what's not in there?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: The funds. So you've got the UBS All China, the UBS China Opportunity, the Hang Seng China Enterprise ETF, and then the BlackRock China bond fund on the fixed income side. None of those show up under a country line because they're domiciled in Luxembourg or Hong Kong.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: So the real number is what?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: I'd need to pull it properly. But it's meaningfully more than the statement suggests. I'd rather give you the exact figure in writing than guess on a call.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Please do. Because this is exactly my problem. I'm looking at a document that's telling me something that isn't true.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: It's not untrue, it's — the statement is doing what it's designed to do, it's just not a look-through view.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Priya, from where I'm sitting that's a distinction without a difference.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: No, you're right. I'll put together a proper look-through on the China exposure, direct plus fund, and send it over.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Thank you. Second thing. The Olam bond.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: The four percent.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: It matures this month, doesn't it? The twenty-fourth or something.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Twenty-fourth of February, yes.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: So what happens? Does the money just land in the SGD account? Do I need to tell you something?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Normally it redeems at par and the proceeds sit in the Singapore dollar current account until we do something with them.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Normally.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: I'll confirm the exact handling and come back to you. I want to check how it's been set up on our side before I tell you something and then it turns out different.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Okay. But please actually come back on that one. Two hundred and fifty thousand nominal is not a rounding error.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Noted. I'll confirm in writing.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Alright. Something else you should know. The Haugen Logistics sale — the second tranche. Deferred consideration.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: The Norwegian business.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Yes. It's confirmed. I don't have a date yet, the lawyers are still going back and forth, but it'll be this year and it'll be around four million US.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That's — okay, that's significant.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: It is. And I don't want it sitting in cash for six months like the Norwegian krone did.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Understood.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: I mean it. That krone balance has been there since — what, twenty twenty-one? Doing absolutely nothing.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: There's the Swedish krona as well.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Right, and why do I have two? I sold one business, in Norway. Where does the Swedish come from?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That would have been the earlier restructuring, I think. I'd have to look.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Add it to the list.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Okay. So — look-through on China, Olam maturity handling, and the origin of the Nordic currency balances.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: And in the meantime I'll put another two hundred and fifty in, probably March. Keep some dry powder ready.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That's helpful, thank you. One thing from my side before I let you go — the Japanese book has been the bright spot. The trading houses, Mitsubishi UFJ. If you wanted to take something off the table there at some point.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Let it run.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Let it run. Understood.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Alright, I'm pulling into the car park. Priya — the two written items. Please.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: You'll have them.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Erik, hi. Sorry, slight delay my end.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: No problem.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Shall we start with the operational bit?

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Yes. I need to move money out. A hundred and eighty thousand US.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Okay. Timing?

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: This week if possible. It's a deposit on a property, the completion date moved up on me.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That's fine, we can do that from the US dollar account. I'll send you the instruction form today — you'll need to sign and send it back, we can't initiate it off a phone call.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Understood.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Is this a one-off or is there more coming?

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: One-off. The rest of the property is funded separately.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Good. Now — I want to raise something and I'd rather do it directly.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Go on.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Your risk profile on file is Very Dynamic. That's the most aggressive category we have. And when I look at what's actually in the account, a very large portion of it is sitting in cash and has been for a long time.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: The Nordic balances.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: The Nordic balances, yes, but not only. The point is there's a gap between the mandate you've signed and how the money is actually invested. If a reviewer looked at this account they'd ask about it.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Is that a problem for me or a problem for you?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Honestly? Both. For you it means you're not positioned the way you told us you wanted to be. For us it's a suitability question we need to be able to answer.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Okay. What do you need?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: A proper investment policy statement review. We sit down, we re-run the risk profiling, and either the mandate changes to reflect reality or the portfolio changes to reflect the mandate.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Fine. When?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: I'd want to do it before the four million lands, not after.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Agreed. Set it up.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: I'll get a date from you once I know the lead time on the risk questionnaire.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: And the Nordic currencies? I asked about those in February.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: You did.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: And?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: I don't have a good answer for you yet.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Priya.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: I know.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: It's been three months. I'm not asking for a research paper. I'm asking why I hold krone and krona, and can we convert them to dollars.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: You can, and I think you should. Let me get the FX desk to quote you properly on both rather than just doing it at whatever the standing rate is. There's close to a million dollars across the two, it's worth getting a proper price.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Then do that.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: I will. Can I put something to you on the income side while we're here?

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Go on.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: You've got a large HSBC position. Nine thousand shares, Hong Kong line. It's a core holding, you're not going to sell it.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Correct.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: So we could write covered calls against part of it. You keep the shares, you collect a premium, and the only risk is that if it rallies hard through the strike you get called away on the portion we've written against.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: How much premium are we talking?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: It varies with the strike and the tenor. On a sensible out-of-the-money strike, a couple of months out — it's not life-changing money, but it's a few thousand Hong Kong dollars for taking a risk you're already comfortable with.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: And if it does rally?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: You sell at the strike. Which on an out-of-the-money call is above where it is today. So you'd be selling into strength, at a price you'd have been happy with.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: I don't hate it. Do I need to approve each one?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Under your current setup, yes. Every option trade needs your written instruction. We can't do it discretionary.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Fine. Bring me specific proposals and I'll say yes or no.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Will do. There's a similar case on Ping An if you're open to it — that one would be a cash-secured put, so slightly different mechanics, you'd be agreeing to buy more at a lower price.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Send me both. In writing, with the numbers.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Yep.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: And China?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Still overweight. You'll have seen the look-through I sent in February.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: I got that, thank you. It was worse than I expected but at least I know.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: My view hasn't changed. I'd want to bring it down. But I'd rather do it into the four million than by selling at these levels.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Meaning?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Meaning if you add four million of non-China assets, your China weight halves without you realising a single loss.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Huh. Alright, that's — yes. Let's plan it that way.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Good. So: withdrawal this week, FX quote on the Nordics, two option proposals in writing, and the IPS review scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: That's the list.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Erik, good morning.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Priya. Right — it's happening.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: The transfer?

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Signed yesterday. Funds go out from the escrow on Monday, so you should see four million US land Tuesday, Wednesday at the latest. Twenty-sixth, call it.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That's excellent news. Congratulations.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Thank you. Now. I said in February I didn't want it sitting in cash and I meant it.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Understood.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: So let's agree what happens to it. Today. On this call. Not in three weeks.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Happy to. I've done the work. Can I walk you through it?

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Please.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: So the headline is we phase it. I don't want to put four million to work in a single day — that's a timing bet and there's no reason to take it. I'd do it over six to eight weeks, in tranches.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Fine in principle. What goes where?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Four buckets. First, Singapore dividend equities — you're barely there. You've got the STI ETF and not much else. I'd add to OCBC, I'd add NetLink for the yield. That's home-market, you understand these businesses, and it's a natural place for a Singapore resident to hold income.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: How much?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Start modest. We're building a position, not making a statement.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Alright. Second?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Gold. You've got the SPDR line already, it's small. I'd increase it. Given how much dollar cash you're about to be holding, having some non-dollar store of value is just sensible.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Agreed. Third?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Singapore dollar fixed income. And this brings us back to something.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: The Olam bond.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: The Olam bond.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Which I asked about in February. And in the email. And I still don't have an answer.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That's on me.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: It's been six months, Priya. The thing was supposed to mature in February. It's August. When I look at the app it's still showing as a holding. Is it matured or isn't it?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: I — that's what I need to check. If it's still showing on the position file then either it hasn't been processed or there's something wrong with how it's displaying.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Those are quite different things.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: They are. I'll get operations to look at it this week.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: This week.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: This week.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Fourth bucket — China.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Reduce it.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That's my recommendation, yes. But as I said in May, the cleanest way is dilution. Add four million of non-China and the weight comes down on its own.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: I hear you, but I want some actual selling too. Not just arithmetic.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Which names?

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: The semiconductor one. SMIC. And honestly the China funds — the UBS ones.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: The funds are the bigger exposure. SMIC is comparatively small.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Then do both.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: The funds will take a bit more thought on timing and tax. SMIC I can action quickly.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Start with what you can action.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: What about Alibaba? I'm down what, fifty-something percent?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Around that.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: I'm not selling it at this level. I'd sooner average down.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That's a view I'd push back on, gently. Adding to a position because it's already down isn't a thesis.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Noted. I still want to do it. Small size.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Then I'd want it recorded as your instruction rather than our recommendation. I'll make sure it's booked that way.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Fine by me.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Now — the options. You sent the proposals in June, I read them.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: And?

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Do them. The HSBC call and the Ping An put. Both.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Both. I'll come back with specific strikes and expiries for your sign-off before I place anything.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Good.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: And the Nordic balances, Erik. I owe you on that too.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Yes you do.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: The FX desk quoted, I have the pricing. I just need your instruction to convert.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Convert them. Both. All of it. Krone and krona into dollars. I've been asking since February.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Understood. I'll get the instruction over to you.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Don't send me an instruction, just — no, fine. Send it. I'll sign it.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: It's a client-directed FX conversion, I can't do it off the call.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: I know. Send it.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: One more thing from my side. The Japanese book — Mitsubishi UFJ is up around eighteen percent. You said let it run in February. Still your view?

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Take some off. Half maybe. Japanese banks have had their run.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Noted.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Last item. The IPS review. We said before the money landed.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: And it hasn't happened.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: It hasn't happened. The risk questionnaire has been reissued internally and I need about ninety minutes with you.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: I'm travelling from the second of September. Before that or after the middle of the month.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: I'll send options.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Right. Let me summarise, because I want to be clear about what I'm expecting.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Four million lands around the twenty-sixth. It gets deployed in tranches over six to eight weeks — Singapore equities, gold, Singapore dollar credit. China comes down, SMIC first, funds after. Small add to Alibaba, my call, my risk. Options on HSBC and Ping An. Nordic cash converted to dollars. Olam bond question answered this week. IPS review booked.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: That's accurate.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: Nine things. I'll be watching the app.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghavan
transcript.text: You'll see the activity as it happens.

transcript.speaker: Erik Haugen
transcript.text: We'll see. Thanks Priya.

messages.body:
Dear Erik,

Thank you for your time yesterday. To confirm the items we agreed:

1. I will prepare a full look-through analysis of your China exposure, covering both directly held securities and fund holdings.
2. I will confirm the handling of the Olam International 4% MTN at its maturity on 24 February and revert in writing.
3. I will review the origin of the NOK and SEK balances.

Noted also your intention to transfer approximately USD 250,000 in March, and that the Haugen Logistics deferred consideration of approximately USD 4m is expected later this year.

Kind regards,
Priya

Priya,

The Olam bond matures today. I haven't had anything from you on it. Can you confirm what is happening with the proceeds?

Erik

Dear Erik,

Please find attached the China look-through analysis we discussed.

The short version: your directly held Hong Kong listed equities represent only part of the picture. Once the UBS All China, UBS China Opportunity, Hang Seng China Enterprise ETF and BlackRock China Bond Fund are included on a look-through basis, aggregate China exposure is materially higher than the country allocation table in your statement indicates.

My recommendation is to reduce this over time. I would not do it in a single transaction at current levels.

Kind regards,
Priya

Dear Erik,

Further to our call yesterday, please find attached the outgoing transfer instruction for USD 180,000 from account 8000223.

Please sign and return at your convenience. We cannot action the transfer without the signed instruction.

Kind regards,
Priya

Signed and attached. Please process this week - completion is on the 20th.

Erik

email_threads.subject: Option proposals - HSBC covered call and Ping An put

messages.body:
Dear Erik,

As discussed on 14 May, please find two option proposals attached.

Proposal 1 - Covered call on HSBC (0005.HK). You hold 9,000 shares. We would write calls against a portion, retaining the shares and collecting premium. Risk is assignment above the strike, i.e. selling into strength at a price above today's level.

Proposal 2 - Cash secured put on Ping An (2318.HK). You would collect premium in exchange for agreeing to purchase additional shares at a lower strike. Cash collateral would be blocked for the duration.

Both require your written instruction before execution. Neither can be actioned on a discretionary basis under your current mandate.

Kind regards,
Priya

Priya,

The Haugen Logistics second tranche is close to signing. I expect approximately USD 4,000,000 to reach the account in the week commencing 24 August.

I want a plan for this before it arrives, not after. Can we speak this week.

Also - I am still waiting on the Olam bond position. It continues to appear on my statement. It was supposed to mature in February.

Erik

Dear Erik,

Thank you for yesterday's call. Confirming the deployment approach we agreed:

- Phased deployment of the incoming USD 4m over approximately six to eight weeks rather than a single tranche
- Build Singapore dividend equity exposure (OCBC, NetLink)
- Increase gold allocation
- Add Singapore dollar fixed income
- Reduce China exposure, beginning with SMIC, funds to follow
- Small client-directed addition to Alibaba, recorded as your instruction
- Proceed with the HSBC covered call and Ping An cash secured put, strikes to be confirmed for your sign-off
- Convert NOK and SEK balances to USD
- Trim Mitsubishi UFJ
- Schedule the investment policy statement review

I am chasing operations on the Olam position and will revert.

Kind regards,
Priya

Good. Funds leave escrow today, you should see them tomorrow.

Please note I have not yet received the FX conversion instruction for the Nordic balances, and I still have nothing on Olam.

Erik

email_threads.subject: Following up - has anything been invested?

messages.body:
Priya,

The four million arrived on 26 August. It is now 16 September. I have logged into the app and as far as I can tell it is still sitting in the US dollar account doing nothing.

I see some small trades have gone through. I appreciate that. But this is not what we agreed on the 21st. We said phased deployment over six to eight weeks. Three weeks have passed and the overwhelming majority of the money has not moved.

I also note:

- The Nordic balances are still in NOK and SEK. I instructed conversion on 21 August.
- The China funds have not been touched.
- I still have no answer on the Olam bond.
- The IPS review has not been scheduled.

This is the third time I am asking about some of these. Please call me.

Erik

Dear Erik,

Thank you for your note and I am sorry for the delay. You are right to chase.

I am pulling together a full status on each of the items you have listed and will come back to you with a complete position rather than a partial one. I would like to arrange a call early next week.

Kind regards,
Priya
